literal: An edict ordered the Crown Prince to oversee the realm; Great Marshal Yaogu accompanied the campaign.
idiomatic: He ordered the Crown Prince to govern in his stead and took Great Marshal Yaogu with him on the march.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinhai day, Hela and others attacked the eastern tribes of Sukunna Mountain and defeated them.
idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month, on xinhai day, Hela and his officers struck the eastern clans of Sukunna Mountain and broke them.

literal: In the eighth month, on yiyou day, they reached Wugu Mountain and sacrificed geese to Heaven.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiyou day, the army came to Wugu Mountain and offered geese to Heaven.

literal: On jiawu day, they halted at the old Xiongnu state, ascended Mount Alidianyadesi, and sacrificed deer.
idiomatic: On jiawu day they encamped in the old Xiongnu lands, climbed Mount Alidianyadesi, and made a deer sacrifice.

literal: On the bingshen new moon of the ninth month, they halted at the old Uighur city and inscribed a stele recording their achievements.
idiomatic: At the bingshen new moon of the ninth month they stopped at the ruined Uighur capital and carved a stone to commemorate the campaign.

literal: On gengzi day, they performed sun-worship in the forest.
idiomatic: On gengzi day they bowed to the sun among the trees.

literal: On bingwu day, cavalry was dispatched to attack the Zubu.
idiomatic: On bingwu day he sent horsemen against the Zubu.

literal: Southern Chancellor Su and Southern Court yilü Dieli raided southwest.
idiomatic: Southern Chancellor Su and Southern Court yilü Dieli swept the southwest.

literal: On yimao day, Su and the others presented captives.
idiomatic: On yimao day Su and his commanders brought in prisoners.

literal: On dingsi day, they cut the Golden River, took stone from Wushan, <3> had it conveyed by cart to the Huang River and Mount Muye, to express the idea that mountains and rivers pay homage to the sea and honor the sacred peaks.
idiomatic: On dingsi day they opened a channel in the Golden River, quarried stone from Wushan, <3> and had it carted to the Huang River and Mount Muye—signifying that every river and ridge bows toward the sea and every peak pays court to the sacred mountains.

literal: On guihai day, the Da Shi lands sent tribute.
idiomatic: On guihai day envoys arrived from the Arab lands with tribute.

literal: On jiazi day, an edict ordered that the old stele of Khan Longbiye be re-carved, recording his achievements in Khitan, Turkic, and Chinese scripts.
idiomatic: On jiazi day he decreed that the old stele of Khan Longbiye be cut anew, its deeds inscribed in Khitan, Turkic, and Chinese.

literal: That month they defeated the various barbarian tribes of Hmusin Mountain, halted at Yedesi Mountain, and sacrificed red oxen and blue horses to Heaven and Earth.
idiomatic: That month they overran the tribal settlements on Hmusin Mountain, camped at Yedesi Mountain, and offered red oxen and blue horses to Heaven and Earth.

literal: The Uighur Boli sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Boli of the Uighurs dispatched envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the bingyin new moon of the tenth winter month, they hunted at Mount Yule, capturing several thousand wild beasts to supply the army's food.
idiomatic: At the bingyin new moon of the tenth winter month they hunted on Mount Yule, taking several thousand head of game to feed the host.

literal: On dingmao day, the army encamped at Mount Balisi.
idiomatic: On dingmao day the army halted on Mount Balisi.

literal: Troops were dispatched across the desert sands; they stormed Fotu City and took all the western border tribes.
idiomatic: He sent soldiers across the drifting sands, stormed Fotu City, and brought every tribe on the western marches to heel.

literal: On the yimao new moon of the eleventh month, they captured Bilie'e, military commissioner of the Ganzhou Uighurs, and then sent envoys to instruct his lord, Khan Wumu.
idiomatic: At the yimao new moon of the eleventh month they seized Bilie'e, the Ganzhou Uighur commissioner, and sent envoys to deliver their terms to his sovereign, Khan Wumu.

literal: They hunted tigers at Mount Wulaxieli and reached Mount Bashishi.
idiomatic: They hunted tiger on Mount Wulaxieli and pressed on to Mount Bashishi.

literal: For more than six hundred li they marched and hunted by turns; fresh meat came every day, and every soldier was fed.
idiomatic: For six hundred li and more they alternated march and hunt; fresh meat came every day, and no man in the ranks went hungry.

literal: In the spring of the fourth year, on renyin day in the first month, victory was announced to the Empress and Crown Prince.
idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, on renyin day in the first month, word of triumph was sent to the Empress and Crown Prince.

literal: In the second month, on bingyin day, Great Marshal Yaogu raided the Xi.
idiomatic: In the second month, on bingyin day, Great Marshal Yaogu harried the Xi.

literal: On dingmao day, the Empress sent Kang Moda to inquire after his health and forwarded imperial robes, wine, and provisions.
idiomatic: On dingmao day the Empress sent Kang Moda to ask after his welfare and forwarded court robes, wine, and a full table.

literal: On yihai day, Xiao Aguzhi returned from raiding Yan and Zhao and presented battle-flags and weapons.
idiomatic: On yihai day Xiao Aguzhi came back from the Yan and Zhao frontier with captured standards and arms.

literal: On xinmao day, Yaogu presented Xi captives.
idiomatic: On xinmao day Yaogu delivered Xi prisoners to court.

literal: In the third month, on bingshen day, the army was feasted at Mount Shuijing.
idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen day, he held a great feast for the army at Crystal Mountain.

literal: In the fourth summer month, on jiazi day, they attacked southward a small barbarian group and took it.
idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on jiazi day, he turned south against a minor tribe and brought it down.

literal: The Empress and Crown Prince came to meet him at Zhali River.
idiomatic: The Empress and Crown Prince rode out to greet him on the Zhali River.

literal: On guiyou day, the Uighur Khan Wumu sent envoys with tribute in thanks.
idiomatic: On guiyou day Khan Wumu of the Uighurs sent envoys with gifts of thanks.

literal: In the fifth month, on jiayin day, he took cool repose at the northern pass of the Shiwei.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin day, he sought the cool of the Shiwei northern pass.

literal: In the ninth month of autumn, on guisi day, he returned from the western campaign.
idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, on guisi day, he came home from the western war.

literal: In the tenth winter month, on dingmao day, Tang reported the destruction of Liang; envoys were at once dispatched in return courtesy.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on dingmao day, Tang announced the fall of Liang, and he immediately sent envoys in reply.

literal: On gengchen day, Japan sent tribute.
idiomatic: On gengchen day tribute arrived from Japan.

literal: On xinsi day, Goryeo sent tribute.
idiomatic: On xinsi day Goryeo sent tribute.

literal: In the eleventh month, on dingyou day, he visited Anguo Temple, fed the monks, pardoned prisoners in the capital, and released the hawks and falcons of the Five Wards.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingyou day, he visited Anguo Temple, feasted the monks, freed the capital's prisoners, and turned loose the hunting birds of the Five Wards.

literal: On jiyou day, Silla sent tribute.
idiomatic: On jiyou day Silla sent tribute.

literal: In the twelfth month, on yihai day, an edict declared: "Of the two matters spoken of, one is already finished; only the hereditary feud with Bohai remains unavenged—how can I remain at rest!
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yihai day, he proclaimed: "Of the two undertakings I foretold, one is complete; only the blood-debt with Bohai remains unpaid. How can I sit idle?

literal: " He then raised an army and personally campaigned against Bohai.
idiomatic: " At once he marshaled his host and marched in person against Bohai.

literal: The Empress, Crown Prince, and Great Marshal Yaogu all accompanied him.
idiomatic: The Empress, the Crown Prince, and Great Marshal Yaogu all went with him.

literal: In the intercalary month, on renchen day, he sacrificed at Mount Muye.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renchen day, he offered sacrifice at Mount Muye.

literal: On renyin day, with blue cattle and white horses he sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at Mount Wu.
idiomatic: On renyin day, with blue oxen and white horses, he worshipped Heaven and Earth on Mount Wu.

literal: On jiyou day, he halted at Mount Sage and shot ghost-arrows.
idiomatic: On jiyou day he encamped at Mount Sage and loosed ghost-arrows against evil.

literal: On dingsi day, he halted at Shang Ridge and by night besieged Fuyu Prefecture.
idiomatic: On dingsi day he reached Shang Ridge and, that same night, invested Fuyu Prefecture.

literal: In the second month, on gengyin day, the prefectures of Anbian, Xie, Nanhai, Dingli, and others, together with circuit military commissioners and prefects, came to court; he comforted them and dismissed them.
idiomatic: In the second month, on gengyin day, the prefectures of Anbian, Xie, Nanhai, Dingli, and the rest, with their commissioners and prefects, came to audience; he received them with praise and sent them home.

literal: The weapons, silks, and other goods taken were bestowed on officers and soldiers.
idiomatic: Arms, silks, and the rest of the spoils he divided among officers and rank and file.

literal: On renchen day, with blue cattle and white horses he sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
idiomatic: On renchen day he again sacrificed blue oxen and white horses to Heaven and Earth.

literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Tianxian.
idiomatic: He declared a general amnesty and changed the reign title to Tianxian.

literal: Because Bohai had been pacified, envoys were sent to report to Tang.
idiomatic: With Bohai subdued, he dispatched envoys to inform Tang.

literal: On jiawu day, he again visited Hurhan City, inspected the treasury goods, and bestowed gifts on his followers according to rank.
idiomatic: On jiawu day he returned to Hurhan City, reviewed the storehouses, and rewarded his followers by rank.

literal: Because the Xi chieftain Boru'en, Wang Yu, and others who had joined the campaign from the Uighurs, Silla, Tibet, Xi, Shiwei, Shatuo, Wugu, and the rest had served meritoriously, they were richly rewarded.
idiomatic: The Xi chieftain Boru'en, Wang Yu, and the allies who had marched with him from Uighur, Silla, Tibetan, Xi, Shiwei, Shatuo, and Wugu lands were singled out for lavish reward.

literal: On bingwu day, the Bohai state was renamed Dongdan, and Hurhan City was renamed Tianfu.
idiomatic: On bingwu day he renamed the Bohai realm Dongdan and Hurhan City Tianfu.

literal: The Crown Prince Bei was invested as Renhuang Wang to rule it.
idiomatic: He invested Crown Prince Bei as Renhuang Wang to govern the new domain.

literal: His younger brother Diela was made Left Grand Minister; Bohai's elder minister was made Right Grand Minister; Bohai's Minister of Works Dae Sagyeon was made Left Secondary Minister; and Yelü Yuzhi was made Right Secondary Minister.
idiomatic: His brother Diela became Left Grand Minister; a senior Bohai minister took the Right Grand Ministry; Dae Sagyeon, Bohai Minister of Works, became Left Secondary Minister; and Yelü Yuzhi Right Secondary Minister.

literal: Within that state, all offenses short of capital crime were pardoned.
idiomatic: Inside the realm he pardoned every crime short of death.

literal: On dingwei day, Goryeo, the Mo tribes, the Iron Lili, and the Mohe and Jurchen sent tribute.
idiomatic: On dingwei day tribute came from Goryeo, the Mo tribes, the Iron Lili, and the Mohe and Jurchen—the last name lost in the manuscript after 鐵驪 (靺鞨).

literal: In the third month, on wuwu day, yilü-bi Kang Mojin and Left Vice Director Han Yanhui were dispatched to attack Changling Prefecture.
idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu day, he sent yilü-bi Kang Mojin and Left Vice Director Han Yanhui against Changling Prefecture.

literal: On jiazi day, Heaven was sacrificed to.
idiomatic: On jiazi day he performed the rites of Heaven.

literal: On dingmao day, he visited the Renhuang Wang's palace.
idiomatic: On dingmao day he called at the Renhuang Wang's palace.

literal: On jisi day, the three prefectures of Anbian, Xie, and Dingli rebelled; Anduan was sent to suppress them.
idiomatic: On jisi day Anbian, Xie, and Dingli rose in revolt, and he sent Anduan to put them down.

literal: On dingchou day, the three prefectures were pacified.
idiomatic: On dingchou day the three prefectures were quiet again.

literal: On renwu day, Anduan presented captives and executed the two rebel commanders of Anbian Prefecture.
idiomatic: On renwu day Anduan brought in prisoners and beheaded the two rebel leaders of Anbian Prefecture.

literal: On guiwei day, he feasted the Dongdan state's officials, distributing gifts by rank.
idiomatic: On guiwei day he banqueted Dongdan's ministers and gave out rewards by station.

literal: On jiashen day, he visited Tianfu City.
idiomatic: On jiashen day he went to Tianfu City.

literal: On yiyou day, the army withdrew; the Bohai ruler led his entire clan westward on the march.
idiomatic: On yiyou day the host turned homeward, with the Bohai king Dae Inseon leading his whole clan west on the road.

literal: On the dinghai new moon of the fourth summer month, they halted at Mount Sanzi.
idiomatic: At the dinghai new moon of the fourth summer month they stopped at Umbrella Mountain.

literal: On xinmao day, the Renhuang Wang led the Dongdan state's officials in taking leave.
idiomatic: On xinmao day Renhuang Wang, with Dongdan's chief ministers, came to bid farewell.

literal: That month, Tang's adopted son Li Siyuan rebelled; Guo Cunqian killed his lord Cun, <4> and Siyuan thereupon ascended the throne.
idiomatic: That month Li Siyuan, Tang's adopted son, rose in rebellion; Guo Cunqian murdered his master Cun, <4> and Siyuan seized the throne.

literal: In the fifth month, on xinyou day, the two prefectures of Nanhai and Dingli rebelled again; Great Marshal Yaogu was sent to suppress them.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinyou day, Nanhai and Dingli rebelled once more, and Great Marshal Yaogu marched to crush them.

literal: In the sixth month, on dingyou day, the two prefectures were pacified.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingyou day, both prefectures were subdued.

literal: On bingwu day, they halted at Shenzhou; Tang sent Yao Kun to announce the national mourning.
idiomatic: On bingwu day the army encamped at Shenzhou while Tang sent Yao Kun to announce the court's mourning.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on bingchen day, Wei Jun, prefect of Tiezhou, rebelled.
idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month, on bingchen day, Wei Jun, prefect of Iron Prefecture, turned rebel.

literal: On yichou day, Yaogu attacked and stormed Tiezhou.
idiomatic: On yichou day Yaogu invested and stormed Iron Prefecture.

literal: On gengwu day, Diela, Left Grand Minister of Dongdan, died.
idiomatic: On gengwu day Diela, Dongdan's Left Grand Minister, died.

literal: On xinwei day, Wei Jun escorted Dae Inseon, the Bohai ruler, west of the imperial capital and built a city for him to dwell in.
idiomatic: On xinwei day Wei Jun convoyed Dae Inseon, king of Bohai, to a site west of the capital and walled a town for his household.

literal: He was given the name Ulugu; his wife was called Aliji.
idiomatic: The captive king was granted the name Ulugu; his consort was styled Aliji.

literal: Zhang Chong, marching-army marshal of Lulong, rebelled and fled to Tang.
idiomatic: Zhang Chong, Lulong's field marshal, rebelled and fled to Tang.

literal: <5> On jiaxu day, they halted at Fuyu Prefecture; the Emperor fell ill.
idiomatic: <5> On jiaxu day the imperial train stopped at Fuyu Prefecture, and the Emperor sickened.

literal: That evening, a great star fell before his tent.
idiomatic: That night a great star plummeted before his pavilion.

literal: At dawn on xinsi day, a yellow dragon was seen coiling above the inner city, about a li in length, its brilliance dazzling the eye, and it entered the traveling palace.
idiomatic: At dawn on xinsi day a yellow dragon a full li long was seen spiraling above the inner citadel, blazing so bright men could scarcely look, before it glided into the traveling palace.

literal: Purple-black vapors shrouded the sky before the sun at last dispersed them.
idiomatic: Purple-black clouds swallowed the sky until the sun broke through and scattered them.

literal: That day the Emperor died, aged fifty-five.
idiomatic: That same day the Emperor died. He was fifty-five.

literal: The prophecy he had made in the third year of Tianzan—"In the bingxu year, at the opening of autumn, I shall surely find my place of return"—was at last fulfilled.
idiomatic: The words he had spoken in the third year of Tianzan—"When the bingxu year comes and early autumn arrives, I shall have my place of return"—were fulfilled at last.

literal: On renwu day, the Empress assumed regency and decided military and state affairs.
idiomatic: On renwu day the Empress took regency and held sole authority over army and state.

literal: In the eighth month, on xinmao day, Kang Mojin and the others stormed Changling Prefecture.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao day, Kang Mojin and his commanders took Changling Prefecture.

literal: On jiawu day, the Empress escorted the coffin westward on the return.
idiomatic: On jiawu day the Empress bore the coffin west on the homeward march.

literal: On renyin day, Yaogu pacified the various prefectures and hurried to the Emperor's camp.
idiomatic: On renyin day Yaogu settled the remaining prefectures and raced to join the mourning camp.

literal: On yisi day, Renhuang Wang Bei arrived afterward.
idiomatic: On yisi day Renhuang Wang Bei came up behind.

literal: In the ninth month, on renxu day, Southern Chancellor Su died.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, Southern Chancellor Su died.

literal: On dingmao day, the coffin reached the imperial capital and was provisionally entombed in the northwest of the inner city.
idiomatic: On dingmao day the coffin entered the capital and was laid in temporary rest northwest of the inner city.

literal: On jisi day, he was posthumously titled Ascendant Heaven Emperor; his temple name was Taizu.
idiomatic: On jisi day he was honored as Ascendant Heaven Emperor, with the temple name Taizu.

literal: In the tenth winter month, Lu Guoyong, military governor of the Lulong Army, rebelled and fled to Tang.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, Lu Guoyong, governor of the Lulong Army, rebelled and fled to Tang.

literal: In the eleventh month, on bingyin day, Southern Court yilü Yelü Dieli, gentleman Yelü Pilu, and others were executed.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingyin day, Southern Court yilü Yelü Dieli, gentleman Yelü Pilu, and others were put to death.

literal: In the second year, eighth month, dingyou day, Emperor Taizu was buried at Zuling; a Zuzhou Tiancheng Army military governor was established to tend the tomb.
idiomatic: In the second year, on dingyou day of the eighth month, Taizu was interred at Zuling, and a Zuzhou Tiancheng Army governor was appointed to keep the tomb.

literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Tonghe, seventh month, he was advanced to Great Sage, Great Brightness, Heavenly Emperor.
idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Tonghe, seventh month, his posthumous title was raised to Great Sage, Great Brightness, Heavenly Emperor.

literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, ninth month, Great Sage, Great Brightness, Divine Fierce Heavenly Emperor was added to his title.
idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, ninth month, he was further styled Great Sage, Great Brightness, Divine Fierce Heavenly Emperor.

literal: The traveling palace where Taizu died stood between two rivers southwest of Fuyu City; afterward the Ascent-to-Heaven Hall was built there, and Fuyu was made Huanglong Prefecture.
idiomatic: The palace where Taizu died lay between two rivers southwest of Fuyu; later the Ascent-to-Heaven Hall rose on that ground, and Fuyu became Huanglong Prefecture.

literal: The encomium states: The forebears of Liao arose from the Flame Emperor; for generations they were the Shenji state; what can be known begins, perhaps, with Qishou.
idiomatic: Thus the historian praises them: Liao's ancestors sprang from the Flame Emperor; for ages they were the Shenji people; the record becomes clear, it seems, with Qishou.

literal: Qishou was born at Mount Du and moved to the banks of the Huang River.
idiomatic: Qishou was born on Mount Du and later settled on the Huang River.

literal: Passing down to Yali, he first established institutions, appointed officials, carved wood for tallies, and dug earth for prisons.
idiomatic: By Yali's time the tribe first fixed laws, set officers in place, carved wooden tallies, and dug earthen cells for prisoners.

literal: He yielded to Zuwu and would not set himself up as ruler.
idiomatic: He stood aside for Zuwu and refused to proclaim himself chief.
